sections.heading: Choosing the Right Business Entity
sections.content: Before starting a business in Bangladesh, it is crucial to select the correct legal structure. The most common forms are Sole Proprietorships (requiring only a Trade License), Partnerships, and Private Limited Companies. A Private Limited Company is the most popular corporate structure as it offers limited liability protection to its shareholders, meaning personal assets are protected from business debts. The Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC) is the sole authority in Bangladesh responsible for the incorporation and regulation of companies under the Companies Act, 1994. sections.heading: Step 1: Name Clearance from RJSC
sections.content: The very first step in registering a company is obtaining Name Clearance. This process is done entirely online through the RJSC website (roc.gov.bd). You must propose a unique name for your company; it is advisable to have two or three alternatives ready. The RJSC system checks the proposed name against existing companies to ensure it is not identical or deceptively similar. Once approved, the name clearance is valid for 30 days, during which you must complete the full registration process, or the name will be released. sections.heading: Step 2: Drafting the MoA and AoA
sections.content: The core documents for any company are the Memorandum of Association (MoA) and the Articles of Association (AoA). The MoA defines the companys constitution, its objectives (what business it will do), its authorized capital, and the details of the initial subscribers. The AoA contains the internal rules and regulations governing the companys management, rights of shareholders, and duties of directors. These documents must be drafted meticulously, usually by a corporate lawyer, and signed by all proposed directors and shareholders. sections.heading: Step 3: Document Submission and Fees
sections.content: After name clearance and drafting the MoA/AoA, the next step is online submission. You will need to upload the signed MoA and AoA, along with details of the directors and shareholders (NID, TIN, photos). For foreign nationals, passport copies and specific investment board approvals may be needed. Based on the authorized capital declared in the MoA, the RJSC system will generate a payment slip for government registration fees and stamp duties. These fees must be paid through designated banks. sections.heading: Requirements for Directors and Capital
sections.content: For a standard Private Limited Company in Bangladesh, the law requires a minimum of two shareholders and two directors (they can be the same people). The concept of a One Person Company (OPC) was also introduced recently, allowing a single individual to form a company. There is no strict minimum paid-up capital requirement defined by law for local companies, but standard practice often starts with an authorized capital of BDT 10,00,000 to BDT 50,00,000 depending on the business scale. faqs.question: Can a foreigner own a 100% company in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes, foreign investors can generally own 100% of a private limited company in Bangladesh, except in a few restricted sectors.

faqs.question: What is a One Person Company (OPC)?
faqs.answer: An OPC allows a single individual to form a limited liability company, simplifying management while retaining corporate benefits. It has specific capital requirements.

faqs.question: Do I need a physical office space before registration?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need a registered address to incorporate the company. You will eventually need an office to obtain the Trade License.

faqs.question: What are the annual compliance requirements?
faqs.answer: A company must hold an Annual General Meeting (AGM), file annual returns with RJSC, and submit corporate income tax returns every year.
